subject: accordion
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a static piano accordion model with an Italian mother-of-pearl aesthetic, figuring out that it can skip joints since it's not articulated, and sketching rough dimensions like roughly 0.45m width for the body.

Now I'm working through the orientation and layout: deciding the player faces +Z with the treble keyboard on the right-hand side and bass case on the left, bellows running between them along X, and reasoning through which face should show the grille versus the bellows folds to match how an accordion actually looks in playing position.

I'll just rest it on its bottom edge sitting flat, like on a shelf, with bellows axis horizontal. Now I'm working out proportions: treble box roughly 0.20 wide and 0.40 tall, bass box 0.08 wide and 0.38 tall, with the pleated bellows connecting them, then laying out x-coordinates for each section so the pieces sit contiguously along the width.

Recentering everything around x=0, I settle on treble spanning -0.26 to -0.09, bellows -0.09 to 0.17, and bass 0.17 to 0.26, with case height 0.42 and depth 0.22. For the bellows I'm planning around 14 alternating pleated folds, likely built as angled extruded boxes rather than a lathe shape.

Rather than extruding a hollow frame (which won't support holes), I'll construct each pleat as a rectangular ridge made of a thin protruding slab, with a solid core box covering the full bellows span, so ridges stick out and valleys recede naturally without needing complex hollow geometry.

I'm worried about frustumBox's axis orientation mismatching width/height since the dimensions differ enough to cause visible errors, so I'm considering a safer alternative: building a square-cross-section frustum using a 4-segment cylinder rotated 45 degrees, scaled to match the desired width and height.

Still working out the geometry math...

The taper ratios differ per axis for an exact inset, so I'll just approximate with a uniform inset ratio of about 0.88 for a deeper visible pleat effect, then move on to defining alternating bellows colors.

For the look, I'm going classic Italian: pearly celluloid body with a mottled swirl of pale pink, aqua, lilac, and cream, deep red/black bellows with white corner trim, a chrome or gold ornate grille, white keys, and pearl bass buttons. I might add a small nameplate detail for an authentic Italian touch.

Structuring the treble case as a beveled pearl box with chrome or gold trim bands around the edges, then adding a 34-key white keyboard along the end face, arranged in a row protruding outward.

I'm working out the keyboard geometry — deciding which face is the grille versus the keyboard side, and figuring out where to place the black keys along the depth axis relative to the player's position.

For the grille itself, I'll put a recessed gold plate on the treble case's front face with a decorative lyre/scroll pattern using slotted openings to show dark behind it, plus register switches positioned above.

Now I'm adding register switches on top of the treble case as a row of small oval switches with pearl inlay, and thinking through the straps—shoulder straps and a bass hand strap—deciding to keep them simple since the back is less visible to the viewer.

For the bass side, I'm laying out the button board on the end face: roughly 60 pearl-domed buttons arranged in 6 columns by 10 rows to approximate the real 120-button accordion layout, with the hand strap placed on the back face where the palm rests.

Actually I'll split each button into a dark metal base ring plus a pearl dome using a hemisphere sphere geometry, rotating it so the flat side faces outward along x. Then I need to figure out the bass-end plate layout with its own buttons and whether the bass case front also needs a decorative grille like the treble side.

I should also add an air button near the top-front corner of the bass case, checking it doesn't collide with the strap or the existing button rows. For the pearl material, I'm designing a custom paint shader that layers mottled noise with normal-based iridescent hue shifts.

Now I'm layering in the decorative details to capture that Italian mother-of-pearl accordion aesthetic: gold filigree grilles with a floral/lyre motif on the treble front, deep ruby red bellows with gold paper corners and white edging, plus metal corner guards and a leather strap with clasp along the bellows pleats.

I'll alternate two frustum colors for down and up pleats, using a deep red and darker maroon, and add a thin cream slab at each ridge edge slightly larger than the frustum for that classic piped-edge look.

Now I'm laying out the bellows geometry: 14 pleats with half-spacing of about 0.0186, positioning ridges and valleys sequentially from a starting x-coordinate so the total run spans 0.26, with ridge height set slightly smaller than the case height to keep proportions believable.

I'm sizing the bellows cross-section with ridge/valley dimensions and checking the lowest point clears the floor, then adding a dark core box inside to hide gaps between the folds before moving on to building the treble case body.

Now I'm detailing the case exterior: the main body box with pearl paint, chrome-and-gold trim plates at the bellows-facing ends, and edge binding strips, using a reusable box helper function to place these parts without needing joints.

For textures, I'm planning a set of 5-12 images: a gold filigree grille SVG for the treble front, and a nameplate reading something like "Bellini · Castelfidardo" placed as a plaque above the grille.

Beyond that I'm sketching a bass-end plate texture, chrome register switches with tiny icon strips on top of the treble, and a pearl inlay flower decal for the bass front face.

Actually simplifying: I'll place the bellows strap directly on the bass case front instead, a small leather tab with stitched texture spanning a few pleats near the bass end, positioned right against the bellows ridge so it reads as a closure strap without blocking the pleat detail.

Now I'm turning to the treble side where the keys are. I'm planning a dark keybed box on the end face that covers the keyboard area, making sure it aligns properly with the front grille so the two pieces wrap together without gaps or overlap issues.

For the 21 white keys, I'm laying them out along the z-axis with black keys positioned toward the player side and raised slightly higher, while the white keys extend forward and sit flush with the bed.

Still working out keyboard geometry...

I'm also planning a treble-side register panel on the case top, with a row of pearl oval switch sliders set into a chrome plate near the back.

Then I'm adding gold trim molding around the top edges of the case, using a simple reusable helper for thin perimeter strips rather than modeling each edge individually.

For the treble front grille, I'm placing a textured plane slightly offset from the case face, sized to the grille cutout proportions, with thin gold frame boxes around it and an opaque dark SVG background behind so nothing shows through. On the bass side, I'm laying out the case geometry with a steel end plate near x=0.26, then positioning the button row just above it, and adding a matching textured rosette plane on the bass front face.

A vertical pearl filigree garland design, using transparent SVG cutouts so the pearl case material shows through around the golden strokes and white blossom outlines, creating an inlay effect centered on the bass face. I'm also considering a tiny tricolor stripe detail for the nameplate, then moving on to the leather straps on the back of the case.

Adding shoulder straps now...

I'll scatter around eight small red and aqua jewel spheres along the trim with a soft glow, treating them as individual parts rather than merged geometry. For textures I'm settling on five or six total—grille, nameplate, register strip, bass inlay, strap leather, maybe a swirl inlay—and keeping the pearl button paint simple using position and normal.

Now I'm working out the case geometry: extruding a rounded-rectangle outline along the thickness axis, with the outline drawn in the z-y plane centered at the case origin, figuring out the bevel direction and extents to get that beveled slab look for the accordion body.

Now I'm adding trim bands around the cases — a slightly larger outline extruded as a thin gold ring near the bellows end, building a helper for rounded-rectangle outlines so I can reuse it for each band's placement along the y-axis.

For the bellows pleat region, I'm positioning trim bands at the treble and bass case ends, centering them slightly offset from the bellows edges so they overlap just enough to hide the seam, then mirroring the bass-side band placement to match the treble side before adding the end trims at the keyboard side.

Now I'm working out the keybed frame structure—gold rails along the top and bottom of the keyboard window, with box dimensions for the rail thickness and length, then defining the z-extent ranges for where the white and black keys sit relative to the bed, making sure the key spans align with the front grille side.

Next I'm positioning the gold frame rods around the grille's rectangular opening, placing them centered on the grille plane with appropriate x,y,z coordinates to form the border.

Then I plan helper functions for boxes and cylinders, add small glowing jewel spheres at the frame corners and plaque ends, and sketch out the grille's decorative SVG texture — a dark background with gold border strokes and a lyre-inspired swirl pattern.

Still writing SVG code...

Skipping feet since cases sit flush at the bottom; I'll add an air valve button at the bass end top plus bass strap loops instead. Now I'm working out the bellows pleat geometry, defining the frustum helper and figuring out how rotating the cylinder maps its top radius to the left side after the axis transforms.

Adding ridge bands and segment coloring...

I'm planning the part budget: merged bands, gold corner studs, pleats, keys, buttons, register tabs, jewels, and rivet rows, aiming for roughly 400 lines of code while staying under a few hundred parts. Setting up paint definitions for pearl, gold, chrome, and brass materials.

Writing pearl shader logic...

Working out the extrude orientation for the case body, setting the thickness axis so the shape is centered, and deciding bevel and smoothing values for the octagon corners. I'm sizing the treble and bass case caps with distinct thickness and center offsets before placing the grille plane on the front face.

Checking whether smoothing level 1 corrupts the octagon's long flat edges—since it cuts corners a quarter of the way along adjacent edges, the longer sides risk getting rounded too aggressively near the corners rather than staying flat.

Deciding to skip smoothing altogether and use a faceted, low-poly chamfer look instead with c=0.02, since the bellows edge and band are hidden under other geometry anyway. I'm now setting up the build structure with merged geometries, using a helper function to combine parts and starting the TypeScript imports for Three.js utilities.

Still writing imports...

I'm sketching out helper functions for this scene: one for creating translated box geometries, a general `put` helper for placing colored parts in model or world space, and plane geometry helpers for textured surfaces with configurable direction and axis orientation.

For a top-facing plane, I'm working out the correct "up" vector so that text or texture on it reads right-side-up when viewed from the front—settling on pointing it away from the viewer to avoid the texture appearing upside-down. I'm also mapping out positions for small details like a grille and bass control buttons on the plate.

Still working out button rotations...

Now I'm positioning the valve buttons in a 6x10 grid with slight stagger and diagonal offset to mimic real accordion rows, and deciding which buttons get darker ebony domes versus pearl ones for visual variety. Then I'm sizing up the air valve cylinder to be noticeably larger than the regular buttons.

I'm adjusting the plate's vertical bounds to fit all rows plus the air button near the top, settling on a range from about 0.03 to 0.40 in y, and repositioning the air button accordingly. I'm also considering a gilt rim frame around the steel-colored plate for a bass-end binding look, and placing the case back wall at the opposite z-end for the strap.

Now I'm working out the back strap: a vertical leather pad centered on the back with stitched texture, chrome buckles, and shoulder strap hangers positioned toward the treble side using small leather band boxes.

I'm skipping the pearl swirl overlay, then placing a chrome register plate on the top treble section and adding a row of seven small pearl switch tabs evenly spaced along it.

Adding texture strip and jewels...

I'll skip the keyboard rail jewels for simplicity and drop unused imports like rng. For the pleat geometry, I'm writing a helper that builds a cylinder-based frustum, rotating it to form the fan pleat shape.

Adding corner guards and merging geometry...

I'm picking ivory and ebony tones for the key colors, dark leather brown for straps, and now writing the SVG grille decoration with layered rounded rects and gold trim.

Still writing SVG code...

Still writing inlay and extrude code...

Positioning the plaque above the grille and setting up the frame rods with gold coloring, then checking that all the box, cylinder, and sphere geometries merge cleanly since they share the same indexed attribute format.
